newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cockerill says small 1996 loss likely.
newsitem.headline: Cockerill says small 1996 loss likely.

text.p: Jean Gandois, chairman of Belgian steel maker Cockerill Sambre, said on Thursday that the company was more likely to make a loss than a profit in full-year 1996.
"Today I cannot say what the results will be. We will probably make a loss but it would not be very heavy for a company of our size," Gandois told a news conference.
"If by good fortune we make a profit, it would not be very great," Gandois said.
He said that normally third-quarter earnings were negatively affected by the fact they followed the holiday season. In the fourth quarter steel prices should stabilise, he said.
"It's possible that the fourth quarter won't give bad results but the third and fourth quarters together may be worse than the first half," he said.
He said that in the second half the distribution and building divisions should give better results and the services division should be positive.
Engineering unit Cockerill Mechanical Industries (CMI) and German car-components unit Ymos AG second-half results "should not be good but should be better than the first half", he said.
